item.title: Microservices vs Monoliths: The Real Trade-offs
item.description:
The microservices vs monolith debate has become almost religious in software engineering circles. Both sides have valid points, but the answer depends entirely on your context.

Start Monolithic

Most successful companies started with monoliths. They’re simpler to develop, debug, and deploy. You can always extract services later when you have clear boundaries and actual scaling needs.

When Microservices Make Sense

Microservices shine when you have:

  • Multiple teams that need independent deployment
  • Different scaling requirements for different parts of the system
  • Clear domain boundaries that map to business capabilities

The Hidden Costs

Microservices introduce distributed system complexity. Network latency, eventual consistency, and debugging across services are real challenges. Don’t underestimate the operational overhead.
